parts.label: (b)
parts.part_stem:
A man travels on a toboggan down a slope covered with snow from point A to point B and then to point C. The path is illustrated in Fig. 1.1.

{{figure:figure_1_1}}

Fig. 1.1 (not to scale)

The slope AB makes an angle of $40^{\circ}$ with the horizontal and the slope BC makes an angle of $20^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. Friction is not negligible.

The man and toboggan have a combined mass of $95\text{ kg}$.

The man starts from rest at A and has constant acceleration between A and B. The man takes $19\text{ s}$ to reach B. His speed is $36\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at B.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the acceleration from A to B.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Show that the distance moved from A to B is $340\text{ m}$.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.part_stem: For the man and toboggan moving from A to B, calculate

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Use your answers in (iii) to determine the average frictional force that acts on the toboggan between A and B.

parts.label: (b)(v)
parts.text:
A parachute opens on the toboggan as it passes point B. There is a constant deceleration of $3.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$ from B to C.

Calculate the frictional force that produces this deceleration between B and C.
